body: A single skate quarterpipe ramp, roughly 3 meters tall and 2.5 meters wide, shown as an isolated game prop in a three-quarter front-left camera angle so both the curved transition face and the flat back support structure read clearly for 3D reconstruction. Welded dark obsidian-black brushed steel frame with visible panel seams and rivet lines along the transition curve. A single continuous electric-cyan neon tube is embedded along the top coping edge, glowing as the ramp's own light source with a soft cyan rim-light bleeding onto the nearby ground. A second thin hot-magenta neon strip traces the bottom kicker edge, marking it as the hazard/grind zone per the park's color language. The ramp surface itself is matte dark obsidian, NOT glowing, so the neon reads as accent lighting rather than a fully lit object. No rider, no character, no other props, no ground plane texture, no cast shadows on a background -- pure isolated object on a flat, seamless, evenly lit white studio background, centered in frame with generous margin on all sides for clean silhouette extraction.

A single tall street lamppost, roughly 4.5 meters tall, shown as an isolated game prop, full height visible top to base in one frame, camera angle three-quarter front-right so the lantern head, pole, and base plate are all distinctly readable for 3D reconstruction. Slender tapering dark obsidian-black brushed metal pole with a heavy hexagonal cast-metal base plate and two acid-lime accent rings banding the pole at the one-third and two-thirds height marks. The lantern head at the top is an angular faceted glass housing glowing warm electric-cyan from within, casting the pole's own dedicated pool of light onto the ground directly beneath it (the park's primary light-source object, per the color language). No character, no other props, no street or ground texture, no background scenery of any kind -- pure isolated object on a flat, seamless, evenly lit white studio background, centered in frame with generous margin on all sides for clean silhouette extraction.

A single stylized night tree, roughly 5 meters tall, shown as an isolated game prop, full height visible top to base, three-quarter camera angle revealing the branch structure's silhouette in depth (not a flat symmetrical front view) for accurate 3D reconstruction. A dark obsidian-black silhouette trunk and angular branching limbs, faceted and low-poly in feel rather than organic-realistic, in keeping with the park's hard-edged graphic style. Clusters of faceted, gem-like leaf canopy in acid-lime with hot-magenta glowing veins running through the facets, reading as bio-luminescent foliage rather than painted leaves -- this is the park's one warm 'nature' color note against the magenta/cyan hardscape. No character, no other props, no ground, no ambient background scenery -- pure isolated object on a flat, seamless, evenly lit white studio background, centered in frame with generous margin on all sides for clean silhouette extraction.

A single skate grind handrail mounted beside a short run of four steps, roughly 4 meters long and descending at a shallow consistent angle, shown as an isolated game prop in a clean side-profile camera angle so the rail's full length, the step edges, and the mounting posts are all unambiguous for 3D reconstruction. Dark obsidian-black brushed steel rail tube on matching black mounting posts, with a continuous thin electric-cyan neon line running the full length of the rail's top edge (marking it as a usable grind surface). The step edges (not the rail) carry the hazard hot-magenta accent line, consistent with the ramp prop's edge-marking language. No rider, no character, no other props, no ground texture beyond the steps themselves, no background scenery -- pure isolated object on a flat, seamless, evenly lit white studio background, centered in frame with generous margin on all sides for clean silhouette extraction.
